evidence_fragments.content: We introduce SepsisAgent, a world model-augmented LLM agent for sepsis treatment recommendation. SepsisAgent uses a learned Clinical World Model to simulate patient responses under candidate fluid–vasopressor interventions, and follows a propose–simulate–refine workflow before committing to a prescription.

Figure 1: Illustration of SepsisAgent’s propose–simulate–refine workflow. Given the current patient state, the agent proposes candidate fluid–vasopressor actions, queries the World Model for predicted patient responses, and commits to a final treatment action based on the simulated trajectories.

On MIMIC-IV sepsis trajectories, SepsisAgent outperforms all traditional RL and LLM-based baselines in off-policy value while achieving the best safety profile under guideline adherence and unsafe-action metrics.

For sepsis treatment, this model acts as an approximate simulator that predicts the physiological consequences of fluid–vasopressor interventions, enabling the agent to compare candidate actions before making a prescription.
Following MedDreamer [19], we use a GRU encoder to encode and update latent representations of sepsis patient trajectories (shown in Figure 2).
We evaluate the Clinical World Model as a predictive simulator and report compact metrics characterizing state prediction accuracy and outcome discrimination (Table 1).
SepsisAgent obtains the best DR and WPDIS scores among all methods, while remaining competitive on WIS.

Stage III further improves both safety metrics, suggesting that the Clinical World Model provides an effective RL training environment for optimizing long-horizon treatment value while preserving clinically safe behavior.

capability_assessments.rationale: LLM treatment policy agent (Qwen3-4B-Instruct) coupled with a learned GRU action-conditioned Clinical World Model via propose-simulate-refine planning and Stage III GRPO agentic RL (L4), evaluated on held-out MIMIC-IV off-policy value and safety metrics (Table 3, Table 4). Caveat: retrospective observational OPE evaluation does not establish causal identification or prospective clinical treatment efficacy.

readiness_assessments.legacy_highest_label: R1 Single-center MIMIC-IV offline OPE validation

limitations: Single-center retrospective MIMIC-IV off-policy evaluation; no external hospital or prospective ICU deployment.

Action conditioning is learned from observational MIMIC-IV trajectories without causal identification; reported L4 policy gains are retrospective off-policy estimates (MIMIC-IV and MIMIC-III cross-dataset), not prospective clinical outcomes.
notes: All 29 physical PDF pages extracted/read; page 2 visually inspected via rendered PNG.

legacy_cells.B: Agentifying Patient Dynamics within LLMs through Interacting with Clinical World Model
legacy_cells.S: How do simulated fluid and vasopressor actions change a sepsis patient's predicted physiology and outcomes, and which dose levels should the agent recommend?
legacy_cells.T: Adults with Sepsis-3 ICU stays in MIMIC-IV; excluded were patients under 18, stays under 24 hours, and cases missing mortality data.
legacy_cells.U: Clinicians / doctors, under whose supervision the authors say any potential clinical use should occur.
legacy_cells.V: Select fluid and vasopressor treatment levels for a patient state.
legacy_cells.AI: Structured EHR clinical variables (demographics, physiology, laboratories, treatment history); missingness masks; treatment actions; patient-context and instruction prompts
legacy_cells.AJ: Two-layer GRU encoder with 128-dimensional hidden state
legacy_cells.AM: Concatenates dynamic features, missingness masks, embedded static features, and embedded treatment actions before temporal encoding
legacy_cells.AN: Forward-fill missing values; use training-set population median when no prior value exists; provide missingness masks to the encoder
legacy_cells.AT: Two-layer GRU recurrently encodes observed state-action history into a history-aware patient representation
legacy_cells.AZ: State consists of explicit clinical variables and a history-aware GRU representation; outputs include predicted physiological variables and clinical outcome signals
legacy_cells.BA: Differentiable Soft Logic layer computes SOFA and SIRS scores from predicted states and Smooth-L1 consistency regularization is used
legacy_cells.BD: Joint fluid and vasopressor dose levels on a 5 × 5 percentile-based grid; vasopressor is norepinephrine-equivalent mcg/kg/min and fluid is total effective volume mL/4h
legacy_cells.BF: Guideline priors specify early crystalloid, MAP target 65 mmHg, and vasopressor initiation if MAP remains below 65 mmHg after adequate fluid; guideline violations are penalized in the reward
legacy_cells.BL: 4-hour steps; trajectory outcome window K = 12 steps (48 hours)
legacy_cells.BN: Clinical consistency regularization through a differentiable Soft Logic layer for SOFA and SIRS; guideline constraints in the agent reward
legacy_cells.BP: 48-hour observation window (K = 12 four-hour steps) for the outcome head
legacy_cells.BS: Predicted next physiological state (Gaussian transition; predicted mean returned to the agent), ventilation status, SOFA/SIRS auxiliary predictions, and longer-term clinical outcome signals including mortality risk
legacy_cells.BT: State-transition head; ventilation-status auxiliary head; SOFA/SIRS consistency heads; outcome head for mortality
legacy_cells.BU: Composite trajectory reward combines terminal survival/mortality, intermediate SOFA and lactate change, and penalties for guideline violations and excessive simulator queries
legacy_cells.BV: World model: Gaussian next-state negative log-likelihood, binary-cross-entropy mortality loss, Smooth-L1 SOFA/SIRS consistency loss, and ventilation loss. Agent: staged supervised fine-tuning, behavior cloning, and GRPO reinforcement learning.
legacy_cells.BY: Qwen3-4B-Instruct backbone (4B as stated in model name)
legacy_cells.CA: Training used 8 H200 GPUs with mixed-precision bfloat16
legacy_cells.CB: Average inference time 6.1 seconds per decision step
legacy_cells.CK: Optimize survival and physiological stabilization while penalizing sepsis-guideline violations; guideline priors constrain fluid and vasopressor recommendations
legacy_cells.DF: Propose–simulate–refine tool interaction; staged supervised fine-tuning, behavior cloning, and GRPO
legacy_cells.DQ: 20,092 ICU stays in the MIMIC-IV cohort; 725 held-out test episodes for LLM-based evaluation; 2,862 MIMIC-III episodes for cross-dataset evaluation
legacy_cells.DX: Clinical World Model: state-transition MAE 0.316; ventilation AUC 0.942; outcome AUC-ROC 0.804 and AUC-PR 0.663
legacy_cells.EC: On the 725-episode held-out test set, SepsisAgent reports DR 10.01, WIS 11.14, WPDIS 23.40, guideline adherence 97.95%, underdosing 0.08%, and overdosing 0.14%; off-policy estimates, not prospective patient outcomes
legacy_cells.EE: Four emergency-medicine experts (two medical doctors and two master's degree holders) manually validated identified failure cases
legacy_cells.EG: Average inference time 6.1 seconds per decision step
legacy_cells.EI: Compared with clinicians, traditional RL, vanilla LLMs, and the Qwen3-4B-Instruct base model; authors report strongest DR and WPDIS and best safety profile for SepsisAgent
legacy_cells.EJ: Compared with world-model-augmented GPT-4.1-mini, Gemini-3-Flash, and o3; trained SepsisAgent outperformed these baselines on the reported overall policy-value and safety results
legacy_cells.EK: Ablations compare Stage I supervised fine-tuning, Stage I+II behavior cloning, and Stage I+II+III reinforcement learning; appendix also compares Transformer, LSTM, 2-layer GRU, and 8-layer GRU world models
legacy_cells.EL: World-model-augmented generic LLMs sometimes greedily followed short-horizon MAP improvements and overlooked longer-term fluid/vasopressor risks; expert-validated overdosing failures were 7.1% for o3 + WM, 7.8% for Gemini-3-Flash + WM, and 10.3% for GPT-4.1-mini + WM
legacy_cells.EM: Guideline-aware priors and guideline-violation reward penalties; unsafe-action rules are separately evaluated and are not optimized during training
legacy_cells.FB: 42 explicit clinical variables encoded into a 128-dimensional history-aware GRU patient representation
legacy_cells.FL: A two-layer GRU encodes patient history and feeds Gaussian action-conditioned next-state and longer-horizon outcome heads. A Qwen3-4B-Instruct policy proposes fluid–vasopressor options, queries the simulator, refines recommendations, and is trained with SFT, behavior cloning, and model-based GRPO.
legacy_cells.FM: Introduces SepsisAgent, an LLM policy trained to use an action-conditioned clinical world model for sepsis treatment recommendations through staged learning and simulated rollouts.
legacy_cells.FN: On retrospective MIMIC-IV test trajectories, SepsisAgent led the compared methods on reported DR and WPDIS and safety measures; world-model-based RL improved policy metrics and patient-dynamics prediction. Cross-dataset MIMIC-III results were also reported.
legacy_cells.FO: The paper states that the work is for academic research, uses retrospective data and simulated environments, is not intended for direct clinical deployment, and any potential clinical use should be supervised by doctors.
legacy_cells.FQ: The authors identify that LLMs are not inherently grounded in patient-specific, action-conditioned clinical dynamics and may fail to estimate how a particular patient responds to a particular dose.
legacy_cells.FR: Evidence is retrospective and off-policy, with simulated model rollouts and cross-dataset evaluation; no prospective clinical deployment or treatment recommendation validation is shown. Action conditioning on observational trajectories is not causal identification.
legacy_cells.FS: Reviewer mapping: M3 Belief-state service; M4 Action service; M5 Dynamics adapter; M8 Planner; M9 Safety & governance
legacy_cells.FT: Reviewer lesson: Ground the language agent in an explicit propose–simulate–refine interface and audit unsupported actions and off-policy evaluation separately.
legacy_cells.FU: Reviewer mapping (KB §20): WMs as substrates for clinical agents
